1 غَبَقَهُ , (S, O, K,) aor.
غَبُقَ (S, O, TA) and
غَبِقَ , (TA,) inf. n. غَبْقٌ; (O, TA;) and ↓ غبّقهُ , inf. n. تَغْبِيقٌ; (TA;) He gave him to drink an eveningdraught, or what is termed a غَبُوق. (S, O, K, TA.) لَا أَغْبِقُ قَبْلَهُمَا أَهْلًا وَلَا مَالًا, in a trad. respecting the companions of the cave [to which allusion is made in the Kur ix. 40], in which the verb is thus written by El-Yooneenee with kesr to the ب, means I did not give to drink to any one [of family nor of cattle] the share [of the evening-draught] of milk of them two. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
